geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the dominant body into a split-wing mass so the access edge can read as a real interstitial public threshold instead of a sealed prism.
Split across the long axis to create a more legible court-like seam in plan.
Open a modest central gap to improve void publicness without fragmenting the mass.
Add a courtyard tied to the dominant mass so the building can support neighborhood public space rather than only a solid object.
Keep the court proportionate and usable as a clear open void.
Face the court toward the access side so the ground response aligns with the verified frontage.
Promote the courtyard-linked split mass as the new root so the public threshold remains in the ancestry of the dominant form.

graph_edits.rationale: Shift the dominant mass away from a sealed compact block toward a more legible public/private split that can expose the access edge.
Increase executable segmentation slightly so the form can register a clearer bend/split without becoming fragmented.
Introduce a small access-side notch to create a legible ground threshold and improve public void read at the frontage.
Align the notch with the program access side so the street edge becomes readable as entry rather than a sealed wall.
Keep the notch bounded and architectural, preserving the dominant mass while opening a usable seam.
Make the entry cut modest but clear enough to register as public threshold rather than decorative clipping.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent single mass across views and the parcel containment reads cleanly, so repair integrity is good. However, the visible form is basically a compact faceted block with a mild bend, and it does not establish the required active street threshold on the verified access edge. The blue frontage is answered by a sealed edge rather than a legible public void, undercut, or entry seam, so void_publicness is weak. The silhouette is not disqualifyingly stair-like, but the section/roof logic remains generic and does not strongly articulate a programmatic ground-public/upper-calm hierarchy for neighborhood living. It is plausible as a small mixed-use object, but not yet convincingly as a neighborhood-living mass with an active street interface and one clear public void or terrace.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More tower-like and urban-commercial than the low-rise neighborhood-living mass here; keep only the clarity of hierarchy, not the scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact prismatic mixed-use massing with a legible base-to-top hierarchy and a strong object presence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more intimate and pavilion-like; the candidate lacks the same void depth and edge activation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Carved-in courtyard/void organization that produces an inhabitable open middle and softer edge condition.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate has only a weak courtyard reading compared with the reference’s strong open-air spatial sequence.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard/terrace atmosphere with spatial permeability and a clearly public ground figure.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Ground-to-tower mass hierarchy and a pronounced base condition that can support mixed-use public life.
